SITE DESCRIPTION
Grainger is a wholesale distributor of maintenance, repair and operations (MRO) products. The Grainger Bordentown facility is located at 400 Bordentown-Hedding Rd., Bordentown, New Jersey. The Grainger Bordentown distribution center consist of an approximate 1.2M ft^2 warehouse facility located within the Central Crossings Business Park, Bordentown Township, New Jersey. The facility was built in 2015/2016 and began operating in March, 2016. 

Bordentown Townships population is estimated at approximately 11,400. The Grainger distribution center and business park is located in an area of mostly undeveloped property with some residential housing located west/northwest of the property. No public water supply wells are located within one mile of the subject property.

STORAGE PROCESS CHEMICALS AND THRESHOLD QUANTITIES
This facility warehouses various products for distribution, including aerosols. The covered process for this facility is: Storage of regulated substances at or above the threshold quantity. The facility stores two chemicals, propane and butane, within a designated aerosol room at quantities above their threshold quantities. These chemicals are present in various aerosol containers in manufacturers original containers and packaging for wholesale purposes. The chemicals are mostly present as the aerosol propellant constituent.

When considering the quantities of the flammable mixture of these chemicals stored within the aerosol room the total weight was considered within the quantities provided. A re-evaluation was performed of the current inventory of aerosol products. Based on the contents provided on safety data sheets (SDS), one flammable category grouping of propane and butane had a calculated quantity that exceeds the threshold quantity of 10,000 pounds. The total quantity of flammable chemicals in inventory was calculated by reviewing the products that met the following criteria:

	Aerosols that contain chemicals covered under the

USEPA RMP program that exceed the threshold quantity.
	Include products where the flammable chemical % was greater than 1.
	Include only items with an NFPA flammability rating of 4
	Exclude any flammable products used for fuel.
	Subtract weight of packaging and container (20%).
	Determined which items have chemicals or groupings of chemicals that exceed the USEPA RMP threshold values.

Based on these calculations, it was determined that one grouping of chemicals (propane and butane) as a flammable mixture has a total weight of 104,000 pounds, exceeded the threshold quantity of 10,000 pounds.

WORST CASE AND ALTERNATE RELEASE SCENARIO CALCULATIONS
Based on these quantities of flammable materials, a worst case and alternate release scenarios were considered and calculated using the United State Environmental Protection Agency RMP*Comp program to complete the off-site consequence analyses. For both the worst case and alternate release scenarios, the single largest vessel size used was determined by considering the largest aerosol in inventory containing propane/butane. The resulting single largest vessel for propane/butane mixture was determined to be a 26-ounce aerosol can of marking paint that weighs 1.628 pounds after removing the packaging/can weight was used for the potential quantity released. The RMP*Comp calculation resulted in a 0.007 mile distance (~47 feet) to 1 psi overpressure for the propane/butane mixture. There are no residential populations within the calculated distance and in a worse case scenario the consequence distance would not extend outside the dedicated aerosol room within the building.

ACCIDENT HISTORY
The facility has been open and in operation for approximately nine years. There have been zero reportable accidents involving a regulated substance (propane/butane flammable mixture) in the covered process (storage) at this facility.

EMERGENCY RESPONSE/EVACUATION PROCEDURES - FIRE
1.	In the event of a fire or fire alarm, notify other ass

ociates in the area either by word of mouth and or by pulling the nearest alarm pull-station. A member of management or Security will contact the fire department by dialing 911. Management or Security is to provide the location of the NEDC (400 Bordentown-Hedding Rd. Bordentown, NJ 08505). All associates should remain calm and remember that safety is the first priority while proceeding to the closest emergency exit.
2.	All associates need to be aware of their surroundings and know the locations of all emergency exits and fire extinguishers.  Note fire extinguishers are in place only to allow egress through emergency exits that may be blocked by fire.  They should only be used if there is not an alternate exit available. 
3.	Any associate that is operating power equipment must stop their equipment immediately, turn it off, disembark and proceed to the nearest emergency exit.  Associates are not permitted to drive any equipment to an exit.
4.	Facilities personnel will, if possible, prior to exiting: a) turn off gas; b) turn off any unnecessary electrical power; and c) monitor the pump house to insure equipment is operating properly.
5.	Upon exiting the closest emergency exit, associates will proceed to their assigned RALLY POINT by using the safest route possible.  Associates should utilize the buddy system while exiting the building and reporting to their assigned RALLY POINT as others may need assistance.
Responsibilities of the Facilities Department:

AEROSOL ROOM FIRE PREVENTION MEASURES
The Aerosol Storage Room was designed per FM Global Data Sheet 7-31, STORAGE OF AEROSOL PRODUCTS. The room contains aerosols stored in two single- and six double-row racks to a maximum height of 32 feet. Each of the racks has twelve 8 foot bays for a total length of 96 feet.  The racks have 6 to 1 tiers.  Aisles between racks are 10.5 feet wide.

Scheme A protection is utilized to protect this room area.  Please see Scheme A at the end of this Executive Summary for the details of

the design.  The horizontal sprinkler layout is in accordance Scheme A, single-row racks and double-row racks, and the vertical spacing of the in-rack sprinkler levels will be a maximum of 10 foot. Four levels of in-rack sprinklers are provided. The sprinkler system is fed from a 150,000 gallon water storage tank and diesel fire pump, which feeds the 12 inch underground fire protection loop for the warehouse.

The Aerosol Storage Room measures approximately 138 x 135 feet (18,635 sq. ft.).   Roll-up fire doors (interlocked with fire alarms) are located at all entrances.  The aerosols include Levels 2 and 3 aerosols, generally within 12 to 16 oz. containers.  Most of the aerosols are within cases/cartons.  

The Aerosol Storage Room has an abundance of sprinkler at four levels within each rack as well as a ceiling automatic sprinkler system.  Each level contains a solid barrier above to contain the heat and smoke within the fire zone. If a fire occurred, several automatic sprinklers will be able to effectively control the fire.  Upon a waterflow alarm or detector the fire door to the room shuts and all smoke, heat and fire is contained within the room.

The Aerosol Storage Room has the highest level of protection per any current code or standard for aerosol storage.
 
DESCRIPTION OF FIRE PROTECTION SCHEME A
A. Provide plywood (minimum 3/8 in. [1 cm]) or sheet metal (minimum 22 gauge [0.7 mm]) barriers and in-rack sprinklers. Use a maximum vertical spacing of 12 ft (3.7 m) between barriers.

B. Install FM Approved K8.0 (K115) or K11.2 (K161), 165°F (74°C) rated, quick-response in-rack sprinklers below each barrier level. Design the in-rack sprinklers to provide a minimum flow of 57 gpm (216 L/min) out of the hydraulically most remote six (6) sprinklers (three on two lines) if one barrier level, or the most remote eight (8) sprinklers (four on two lines) if two or more barrier levels are provided.

C. If there are adjacent bays of rack arrays not dedicated to aerosol p

roduct storage, provide a noncombustible, solid vertical barrier (e.g., 22 gauge (0.7 mm) sheet metal) in each longitudinal and transverse flue space to separate the aerosol product storage from adjacent bays. For double row racks with aerosol products storage on only one side of the rack, treat the side devoted to the storage of aerosol products as a single-row rack, with fire protection provided. Protect the adjacent side based on the commodity stored in that area.

D. A vertical chain link fence may be used in lieu of a solid vertical barrier if the entire rack is protected with Scheme A.

E. Ceiling sprinkler demand does not need to be included in the hydraulic calculations for in-rack sprinklers. Calculate the water demand at the point of supply separately for in-rack and ceiling sprinklers. Provide a 500 gpm (1900 L/min) hose stream allowance in the hydraulic calculations for the in-rack sprinkler protection.  Provide the combined fire protection water demand for a 1-hour duration.

F. Design ceiling sprinklers to protect the surrounding occupancy, but not less than 7 psi (0.5 bar) using twenty (20) K8.0 (K115) sprinklers. If the aerosol product storage does not extend to the full height of the rack, protect the other commodities stored above the barrier in accordance with appropriate data sheets as if the entire rack height was filled with that commodity. If in-rack sprinklers are required for the other commodities, each level of barrier and in-rack sprinklers can be given credit as a level of in-rack sprinklers.
